findings.text: _sprint_holds_item re-implements the row-slug extraction that reckon/_store.py:3468 sprint_item_slug already owns, and drops that owner's path-spelling fallback and whitespace strip, so the new read-back predicate can disagree with the module that owns the item shape about what a sprint holds.

the resource_edit_error branch returns ok=false with no applied field, so a move refused before any write (for example the item already in the destination) leaves the applied verdict unstated, and the fragment's claim that a refused resource edit carries applied:false holds only for the ProjectStateError branch at line 1750.

the not-applied branch retires the journal, deleting its before-bytes, and then raises without restoring either sprint, so on the one path where the read-back disagrees with the two writes the item can be left in both sprints or neither with the recovery journal already gone, against the plan's all-or-nothing requirement.
